messages:
leo_customer: Hey team — our org (org_id: org_42xyz) hit 0 credits around 2025-11-30 19:00 local and the UI still shows 'resets in 6 hours' but we expected a refill at midnight local. Can you confirm when monthly credits reset? We're seeing calls failing with 429 and `quota_exhausted` error.

marie_support: Sorry you're hitting this, leo. Can you paste one of the failing request IDs? Also which timezone is your billing/org set to?

leo_customer: request_id: req_20251130_7b3a9, examples: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"x-large","input":"test"}'` -> 429. Our account billing contact says timezone = America/Chicago.

marie_support: Thanks. Quick checklist from our side: 1) hosted monthly refill runs at 00:00 UTC (server-side) for all tenants, 2) UI shows local converted time which can be confusing with DST, 3) if a tenant consumed burst credits earlier in the day and used up the monthly pool, they'd see 0 before local midnight.

leo_customer: Okay but we definitely had credits remaining the night before. They dropped suddenly after a big ingestion job at ~18:50 local. Shouldn't there be a burst window or pro-rata buffer?

dave_billing: Adding context: monthly credits are allocated once per cycle at 00:00 UTC. We do allow a small burst buffer on some plans, but that buffer is not guaranteed and can be consumed by large sustained usage. If the customer used a high-throughput batch run, the monthly pool + buffer can be exhausted earlier.

leo_customer: Can you check whether the refill happened at 00:00 UTC on 2025-12-01 for org_42xyz?

srebot: Automated check: refill_job_run for cycle=2025-12-01 started at 2025-12-01T00:00:03Z, status=completed, tenants_processed=12,345.

marie_support: SRE bot confirms the scheduled job ran at 00:00:03Z. That means the tenant should have been credited then. Two hypotheses: 1) credits were consumed after the refill due to background ingestion, 2) there's a display/caching lag in Console/usage UI.
\
leo_customer: Hmm, our logs show consumption spike at 2025-11-30T23:50:00-06:00 (which is 2025-12-01T05:50:00Z). That's after midnight UTC. So maybe we used the new month's credits immediately. But UI still said reset in 6 hours earlier. So UI mismatch + billing confusion.

marie_support: That timing explains it — your job kicked off after 00:00 UTC, so it consumed credits from the new cycle. The earlier UI message 'resets in 6 hours' was from client-side local tz conversion before DST offset changed for that tenant's browser cache. We're going to: (A) verify credit ledger entries, (B) check for UI caching bug, (C) advise on guardrails to prevent large batch consumption.

leo_customer: For (C) what do you recommend? We need a way to avoid surprise full-month depletion from nightly ETL runs.

tara_engineering: Recommended mitigations: 1) Use rate limiting / request throttling in your batch job (we can suggest a pattern), 2) set a per-key quota with our API keys (create an application key with a daily cap), 3) schedule large pipelines to run before UTC midnight if you want them to charge against previous cycle, or after if you expect fresh credits. Also we can create a dedicated Dedicated reservation if you want guaranteed capacity.

leo_customer: Can you show an example for adding a simple token-based throttle?

tara_engineering: Example snippet (pseudo):
```
# naive rate limiter for bash + curl
for i in $(seq 1 $N); do
  sleep 0.2  # 5 rps
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
done
```
Or use worker pools with concurrency=4 and per-worker sleep to stay under desired RPS. We'll also share a link to a sample repo.

leo_customer: Cool. Back to the immediate issue — can we get a one-time top-up while we change pipeline scheduling? Our account is on growth plan.

dave_billing: I can issue a one-time emergency credit top-up of 5M tokens for org_42xyz pending review. I'll need the billing contact email and confirmation.

leo_customer: billing@acme-example.com — please confirm ETA.

dave_billing: ETA for manual top-up: ~30 minutes after approval. I'll also attach a ticket (BILL-12345) and add notes about recommending a reserved capacity option.

marie_support: Action items for support/eng: 1) Verify ledger entries and confirm top-up applied (assigned to @kai_oncall), 2) Create console doc clarifying 'reset time = 00:00 UTC' and DST caveats (assigned to @marie_support), 3) Engineering to investigate caching edge where UI shows stale 'resets in X' for some tenants (assigned to @tara_engineering).

kai_oncall: I'm checking ledger now for org_42xyz... Found entries: 2025-12-01T00:00:03Z credit +10,000,000 tokens (monthly), 2025-12-01T05:50:20Z consumption -10,500,300 tokens (batch job). So the credits were consumed after the refill; no backend refill failure.

leo_customer: That matches our logs. Thanks for confirming. Please do the top-up while we retool the ETL.

dave_billing: Top-up BILL-12345 applied at 2025-12-01T06:12:00Z +5,000,000 tokens. Please verify on your side.

leo_customer: I see the tokens now, requests are succeeding again. Thank you everyone. :tada:

marie_support: Closing loop — we'll follow up with documentation updates and a console cache invalidation check. If anything else pops up ping this thread or DM.

kai_oncall: Note for postmortem: consider adding a per-tenant consumption alert that triggers when >50% of monthly quota consumed within a 2-hour window. Filing follow-up (ENG-5498).

leo_customer: Appreciate it. We'll also look into running the nightly at a different hour.

srebot: Incident note logged: INC-2025-431; no system outage; customer self-inflicted high consumption; billing top-up applied.
